prompt: Design login security for a consumer account service that currently supports email/password and recovery email. Add optional passkeys without making recovery the weakest path. Define password-verifier requirements, compromised/common-password screening policy, anti-enumeration and credential-stuffing throttling, WebAuthn RP/origin/challenge/user-verification checks, passkey enrollment and duplicate handling, recovery codes, lost-device recovery, authenticator replacement/removal, and fresh-authentication requirements before changing the primary email, resetting all authenticators, or exporting recovery material. Explicitly state what is and is not phishing-resistant and what happens to existing sessions after account recovery or suspected compromise. Leave OAuth/OIDC federation out of this scenario.

requirements: consumer account with email/password, recovery email, and active sessions
WebAuthn-capable RP fixture with valid/invalid origin, RP ID, challenge, credential, and user-verification cases
lost-device, recovery-code, and authenticator-replacement lifecycle fixtures

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The design specifies password-verifier storage, compromised/common-password handling, and throttling/anti-automation dimensions without depending on revealing account existence or a single attacker-controlled global lockout key.
Passkey/WebAuthn verification explicitly validates challenge freshness, RP ID/origin, credential identity, signature, and required user-verification state before establishing authenticated state.
Recovery, backup-code, lost-device, and authenticator-replacement flows have explicit assurance requirements and cannot silently bypass the stronger authenticator policy.

Primary-email change, authenticator reset/removal, and recovery-material export require appropriately fresh authentication or the deliberate recovery path, not merely possession of an old ambient session.
The account-recovery/compromise path defines which existing sessions or refresh credentials are revoked, rotated, or retained and records the relevant security event.
